title: Cell-specific mitochondria affinity purification (CS-MAP) from Caenorhabditis elegans
protocol: Harvest synchronized adult animals.
Wash harvested animals with two successive volumes of 7.5 mL M9 buffer using a pipettor.
Transfer washed animals to a 15 mL Falcon conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 2 minutes.
Replace the supernatant with 14 mL fresh M9 buffer.
Wash the pellet once more with 7.5 mL of fresh M9 buffer.
Centrifuge again at 200 × g for 2 minutes.
Replace the supernatant with 14 mL fresh M9 buffer to remove as much OP50 from the sample as possible.
Rotate the animals in 10 mL of M9 buffer for 30 min at 30 RPM at 22°C–25°C.
Pellet the animals by centrifugation at 200 × g for 2 min.
Wash the pellet once more with 14 mL of M9 buffer.
Pellet the animals by centrifugation at 200 × g for 2 min.
Replace the M9 supernatant with 14 mL of ddH2O to remove traces of the M9 buffer.
Centrifuge again at 200 × g and remove the ddH2O supernatant.
Keep the sample on ice for less than 1 h.
Suspend the sample in 1.5 mL of cold Mitochondrial Isolation Buffer (MIB) with protease inhibitor cocktail.
Transfer the sample with a 1 mL tip and a micropipette into a cold 7 mL Dounce tissue grinder tube.
Prewash the pipette tip with a mild detergent if necessary.
Transfer animals into the Dounce tissue grinder tube in successive volumes of 300 μL to minimize adherence to plastic walls.
Perform 20 to 30 Dounce tissue grinder strokes.
Push the pestle towards the bottom of the Dounce reservoir parallel to the tube during each stroke.
Twist the pestle before reaching the bottom and pull it out of the buffer, maintaining a parallel position to the tube walls.
Ensure strokes are regularly spaced, relatively fast, and go in and out of the buffer for each individual stroke.
Experience medium to strong resistance against the sample during douncing to ensure proper homogenization.
Critical: Extract mitochondria from tissues using 20 to 30 strokes with a glass Dounce tissue grinder.
Wash the Dounce tissue grinder with demineralized water between each individual sample to prevent erosion and cross-contamination.
Meticulously wash the Dounce tissue grinder with demineralized water after each experiment, then air-dry before storage.
Consider using a new Dounce set if results become inconsistent due to wear.
Homogenize animals synchronized at L4 larval stage to adulthood for more efficient extraction.
Transfer the homogenate into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Gently mix the homogenate by pipetting a few times up and down with a volume of 300 μL using a 1 mL tip.
Save 300 μL of the homogenate as Input 1 (whole animal homogenate).
Centrifuge Input 1 at 12,000 × g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant from Input 1.
Freeze Input 1 at -80°C for later processing.
For metabolic assays, keep Input 1 on ice and process directly at the end of the CS-MAP procedure.
Remove intact animals, animal fragments, and large pieces of cellular debris by centrifuging the remaining homogenate at 200 × g for 5 min.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube after low-speed centrifugation.
Centrifuge the supernatant further at 800 × g for 10 min.
Transfer the supernatant from this second centrifugation to a new 1.5 mL tube as crude animal homogenate.
Save a small aliquot of the crude animal homogenate as Input 2 if needed.
Pellet the enriched mitochondrial fraction within the crude animal homogenate by centrifugation at 12,000 × g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 20 μL of MIB to the enriched mitochondrial fraction.
Resuspend the enriched mitochondrial fraction in MIB by vigorously pipetting the solution up and down for 1 min using a P20 micropipette.
Assess the quality of the enriched mitochondrial fraction using a fluorescence microscope.
Pipette 1 μL of the sample onto a glass slide.
Cover the sample with a coverslip.
Observe the sample under a fluorescent compound microscope using a 40× oil objective (EC Plan-Neofluar 40×/1.30 Oil DIC M27).
Select the red channel (excitation wavelength 587 nm, emission wavelength 610 nm, light source intensity 50%, exposure time 3 s, binning mode 2.2).
Calibrate the microscope's 587 nm red channel to background fluorescence levels using wild-type animals that have undergone the same CS-MAP procedure.
Ensure appropriate microscope settings are used to avoid misidentifying irrelevant background dots as mKate2-positive mitochondria.
If no fluorescent mitochondria are observed, restart the procedure.
Pipette the enriched mitochondrial fraction up and down with a P20 micropipette for 1 minute.
Observe 0.5 μL of the sample under the microscope to check for clumps.
If clumps are observable, pipette the sample up and down an extra 20 times.
Incubate the enriched mitochondrial fraction with anti-HA magnetic beads on ice or at 4°C.
Add 400 μL of cold Phosphate EDTA BSA buffer (PEB) with protease inhibitor cocktail to the 20 μL of MIB-suspended enriched mitochondrial fraction.
Homogenize the sample by vigorously pipetting up and down 10 times using a P200 micropipette set to 200 μL.
Transfer the contents into a 0.6 mL round-bottom microtube.
Carefully wash 100 μg of anti-HA magnetic beads in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube by adding 1 mL of cold PEB with protease inhibitor cocktail and flicking gently to mix.
Place the microcentrifuge tube into a standard magnetic rack and leave for 1-2 min until the magnetic beads have assembled against the magnet.
Carefully remove clear PEB before removing the tube from the magnetic rack and repeating the washing process at least 6 times.
Resuspend the clean anti-HA magnetic beads in 100 μL of PEB with protease inhibitor cocktail.
Use 100 μg of anti-HA magnetic beads per sample for purification.
Wash the magnetic beads as required and add them to the 400 μL sample in 100 μL of PEB with protease inhibitor cocktail.
Wrap Parafilm around the closed lid of the tube containing the mixture.
Incubate at 4°C under gentle rotation using an Intelli-Mixer RM-2 on program F1 at 8 RPM for 1 hour.
Pipette up the sample carefully and position the tip into the magnetic field of the magnet adjacent to one flat surface of the magnet on the PCR rack of the homemade CS-MAP device.
Allow mitochondria attached to magnetic beads to aggregate on the wall of the tip closest to the magnet for 1 minute.
Carefully remove the micropipette from the tip without disturbing the magnetic bead pellet.
Aspirate 25 ml of cold PEB using a pipettor and a 25 ml plastic serological pipette.
Plug the tip of the 25 ml pipette into the top of the 1 ml tip.
Carefully unplug the pipette from the pipettor without disrupting the 1 ml tip or magnet.
Allow the PEB to flow through the 1 ml tip and into the waste bucket.
Reattach the pipette to the 25 ml pipette if an air bubble forms in the 1 ml tip, aspirate less than 1 ml of liquid briefly to clear the bubble.
Unplug the pipette from the pipettor once again.
Once all the PEB has passed through the column, remove and discard the 25 mL pipette.
Remove the 1 mL tip from the magnetic field.
Place the 1 mL tip into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing beads.
Elute the bead pellet by adding 1 mL of PEB into the tip.
Reconnect the P1000 micropipette to the tip containing the beads.
Pipette up and down several times to resuspend the beads.
Using a standard magnetic rack, pellet the magnetic beads.
Replace the PEB used for elution with 1 mL of fresh PEB.
Vortex the sample three times for 2 seconds each.
Place the tube under gentle rotation for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Perform a second wash with 25 mL of cold PEB on the CS-MAP homemade setup.
Remove PEB using a standard magnetic rack.
Resuspend the immunomagnetic-purified (IPed) mitochondria in 20 μL of cold MIB with protease inhibitor cocktail.
Keep the sample of immunomagnetic-purified (IPed) mitochondria on ice.
